architecture:
GOAL. React owns every element of every page except raw drawing surfaces. Static markup is server components split into reusable components; every element a script writes today is rendered by a client island from state; page-wide state lives in module-scope stores read through hooks; canvas 2D, D3, ECharts, deck.gl and globe.gl draw only inside refs handed to them by hooks (or, on Week 3, by the corridor engine that hooks register surfaces with). Readers see the same pages: built HTML equals main after tests/built-page.mjs normalise() on every batch (zero static diff), and runtime DOM, text, storage, URL, focus, scroll, canvas and ECharts output, console and requests match main under scripts/parity. Happy paths match main exactly; failure paths follow the isolation mandate (section 4).

1. COMPONENT KINDS
(a) Server markup components (src/components/{site,post,arcade,week03,week04,week05}): no 'use client'; attributes in the order today's JSX writes them; `{" "}` text nodes reproduced; owner undefined omits data-owner, "" emits it; ids explicit props, never useId. P3 surveys every occurrence of each shape on every built page (review/react-migration/shapes.md) and gives post/ and site/ components props that cover them; a prep batch that meets a shape they cannot express writes a page-local component in src/components/<week>/ or its feature folder and never edits post/ or site/.
(b) Islands: 'use client' components exported only through island(name, Component, Placeholder, { roots, affects }) from src/lib/island.tsx. An island renders exactly the server markup at its spot on the server and on the first client render, and the content today's script writes once useHydrated() is true and its data is ready. Islands never receive children. roots = CSS selectors of every element it renders ('none' for service islands); affects = selectors of other islands' elements that legitimately change when it fails, or 'page' for drivers (Week 3 engine driver, Week 4 router and frame services, Week 5 frame compat). island() registers {roots, affects} in globalThis.__ISLANDS__ only when __PARITY_FAULTS__ is defined. Names '<page>/<feature>/<Name>'.
(c) Shells: 'use client' *Shell.tsx that wrap server children and only add attributes or handlers from stores (Week 4 topic/panel details, rail items, toc links, mockup cards). No data, vendor, chart or canvas hooks, no throw. Shells are not boundaries (catchError passes the fallback props without children).
(d) Slots: each prep batch puts every element a script touches behind a component in src/features/<page>/<feature>/slots*.tsx. Slot files stay server files; a feature batch converts a slot by re-exporting an island from a separate 'use client' file in its folder. Coverage is checked mechanically: scripts/parity/touched.mjs records every element main's scripts look up, listen on or mutate, and slot-coverage.mjs checks each lies inside a selector listed in slots*.json.
(e) Terms on server prose: TermProse (server) converts its JSX children into a JSON tree (host elements, strings with every JSX string child kept as its own text node, server function components expanded by calling them, <Term> encoded) and renders the Termified island, which renders the tree plain on the server and first client render and, after hydration and once every file in `after` is loaded (as main awaited it), the tree passed through termifyTree(tree, terms): termify's rules (NO_TERM list, first indexOf inside one text node, document order, one term per call, calls in order). Script-built strings use <Term> in JSX or TermText.

2. RUNTIME MODULES
- src/scripts/runtime/store.js createStore(initial) -> {getState, getInitialState, setState, subscribe}; data.js loadJSON/peekJSON/subscribeJSON (one request per href, evicted on rejection); vendor.js loadVendor(file) (one script per URL, reuses an existing <script src>, evicts on error); owned.js markOwned/isOwned (transitional); islands.js registerIsland/faultPoint (Node-testable).
- src/lib: useStore, useHydrated, useData(url|null, {enabled, throwOnError}), useVendor(file, global, {enabled}), useElementSize, useFittedWidth, useCanvasPaint/useCanvasStage, useEChart(hostRef, {option, notMerge, onEvents, enabled, renderer}) with renderer required, useEChartsMap, useDeck, useGlobe, useTypeScale, useTokens, useTextMeasure, useBodyDataset/useBodyClass (monotonic, no cleanup), useDocumentEvent, useOutsideClose(refs, onClose, {escape}) (ref.contains, never stopPropagation), useOwnedRef (markOwned in a ref callback), island/useThrowToBoundary/report, ChartTip (one persistent body div, hidden attribute toggled, positioned in a layout effect with corridor.js's clamp maths).
- src/components/post: Term, TermLayer (Week 4 only), SegmentedControl, TermProse, Termified; src/scripts/week04-ui.js termifyTree, splitTerm, NO_TERM.
- src/kit (K1b/K2): StripChart, MiniStrip, Table, DecoratedTable, Figure, EChart, Concordance, Passage, wikiLink, TermText, TipBox, HoverTipHost, palette, NetworkView.

3. STORES. Module-scope plain-JS stores (src/features/<page>/<feature>/store.js) read with useStore; no page-level providers, so nothing above the prose holds state or can throw. getServerSnapshot = initial state = what the server rendered. URL, storage, matchMedia, computed style and location-derived URLs are read only in effects or after useHydrated(). Static export never navigates client-side (plain <a>), so module scope equals page lifetime.

4. ERROR ISOLATION
- island() wraps the island in catchError(Fallback) (bundled docs 01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/catchError.md). Fallback(props) renders Placeholder(props), the island's server markup, and logs once through report(): console.error('a page script failed', name, error). Render and effect errors reach the boundary; shared hooks (canvas, ECharts, deck, globe, data with throwOnError, vendor) try/catch their own work and rethrow through useThrowToBoundary; faultPoint('render') fires after hydration and faultPoint('effect') in the wrapper's mount effect.
- Expected async failures are states that render main's exact text in the failing island's own hosts (#status, #place-status, #methods-status, #jobs-status, #app-status, #signal-load, #v-status, #years-status, .w4-vis-error, errorInto paragraphs, entities' status). Optional files keep .catch(() => null).
- Failure-path policy: on the happy path every page equals main. Where main couples failures (week05-frame Promise.all of six files, week04-frame of five, week04-vis-intros 187/482/503, week04-vis-staffing 377, week05-search 119 for its two files, corridor.js main() and its sequential repaint calls, the Week 3 drawer install order), the rewrite isolates per independent chart, as the owner mandated; each such place has an FP id in knownBugsPreserved and an expected-diff entry in known/<page>/faults-<batch>.json. page.route aborts every request to a URL, so under injected faults main's three week04_place.json fetches fail exactly like the deduped one; the shared cache only couples transient failures (FP09).
- Body/html writes never clean up (main never removes them), so a faulted island cannot strip data-skin or body.unlocked. Event-handler errors stay uncaught, as on main.
- Proof per batch: faults.mjs --data (expected table) and --islands (roots equal their JavaScript-disabled markup, outside ids unchanged unless listed in affects, main keeps its children, server text still present, 'a page script failed' logged).

5. DATA. useData(asset(path)) after hydration, one request per URL (the harness allows head <= base). Lazy loads keep their trigger: Week 3 drawers on first open; Week 4 methods, entities, years, roles, skills, radar and pagerank on first panel open (years and roles retry on the next open after a failure, skills does not). No server-to-client data props, no build-time JSON in HTML.

6. VENDOR. Only loadVendor/useVendor; files stay in public/assets/vendor (ECharts 5.5.1, D3 7.9.0, globe.gl 2.32.0, deck.gl 9.0.30). From P2a every legacy loader delegates to loadVendor, because islands may inject a vendor first and a second execution would replace window.echarts. ECharts renderers stay as main initialises them (kit 'svg'; the others as their modules do); the harness records the renderer type.

7. TOOLTIPS AND TERMS. Corridor charts use ChartTip; kit charts TipBox; HoverTipHost reproduces week05-frame hoverTips including history (tipAttached false after a redraw that empties the host, true after a hover, re-appended last), checked against fixtures captured after load, hover and resize over three runs. ECharts, deck and globe keep native tooltips. Terms: static <Term>; server prose TermProse/Termified; script-built text <Term>/TermText; only Week 4 mounts TermLayer.

8. HYDRATION RULES. No window, document, location, storage, matchMedia, getComputedStyle, Date.now or Math.random in render; url()/asset()/SITE values rendered only after useHydrated(); first client render equals the server render; no useSearchParams (client-renders to a Suspense boundary under output 'export', bundled docs use-search-params.md), usePathname, useRouter, next/link, next/dynamic, React.lazy, Suspense or use(); <details> never controlled; controlled inputs hold the raw string. Enforced by static.mjs, react-rules.test and the runtime console check (hydration warnings fail).

9. WEEK 3 CORRIDOR ENGINE. corridor.js keeps main's renderer model: R keys globe, map, hist, ccdf, scatters (calls scatterBetween and scatterZ, line 1966), scatterBetween, scatterZ, prestige, denmark (dk-time, dk-rank, dk-nordic plus panels), setupGlobe, setupMap; cartography is canvas-only, drawn by renderTypology. W3-P1 writes RENDER_KEYS (R key -> canvas ids) and pure painters paint<Name>(ctx, size, S) -> {marks, table, note}; W3-P2 writes the *Model builders, PAINT_TRIGGERS (event -> ordered R keys and non-R draws, copied from the call sites setYear, select, enablePicking hover, setupMap hover, syncFlow timer, earthTexture ready, globe drag, restyle, resize, axis clicks, renderTypology) and exports every top-level pure function and constant. W3-1 replaces the orchestrator with corridorStore/hoverStore, an engine (src/features/week03/core/engine.js: R table with installRenderer's fill-the-gaps merge, surface/host registries, per-chart picking marks, dispatch(event) running PAINT_TRIGGERS with per-key try/catch (FP05), LOAD_SEQUENCE of main()'s steps), an api facade composed from per-folder parts (variants, drawers and window.api see main's api shape through a write-through state Proxy), a driver island, and bridge files that hold main's DOM writers unchanged in the folders of the batches that will replace them. The page works at every step, the legacy variant contract keeps running until W3-2 hands React host descriptors, and canvases register as surfaces when their islands land.

10. DECIDED SHAPES (details in the batches): Week 4 deep dive (deepDiveStore, resolveRoute, uncontrolled details shells, router island with hash/popstate, resize broadcast kept, data-want rendered from the store); Week 4 frame (rail shell + spy, TermLayer, compat services that observe with MutationObserver and skip owned nodes); place (placeStore, usePlaceData, registerMap once, Reset view buttons portalled after init); entities (lazy deck island); staffing (StaffingNum islands); questions (one island per host); arcade (logbookStore, ArcadeChrome, LogbookDialog, Prediction, useRevealHash, collection store with resumable mulberry32, transit closure reducer, Ride); NetworkView (JSX + d3-zoom on the svg ref); signal (reducer + BaymaxMap); mockups (gallery store, card shells, viewer); screen-test (canvasStage canvases, rig rAF, Math.random order kept).

11. FILE LAYOUT. src/lib (hooks, island, ChartTip, README.md rules/recipes/gates); src/scripts/runtime; src/components/{site,post,arcade,week03,week04,week05}; src/kit; src/features/<page>/<feature>/ (islands, shells, slots, store.js, bridges); src/app/(<page>)/.../_sections/*.tsx; src/scripts/*.js keep every test-read literal and pure builder at its current name; scripts/parity (harness, scenarios, known, fixtures); review/react-migration (map.json, shapes.md, known-bugs.md, requests/).

12. TRANSITION. Each page converts on an integration branch (react/<page>) and reaches main in one owner-approved PR that deletes its entry and imperative modules. react/week05, react/week04 and react/week03 are cut from main only after Stage 3 (kit and template) has merged; react/arcade and react/leaves after Stage 2. A converted module becomes side-effect-free so its entry line is a harmless import; bridges (`// bridge: <close batch>`) and shims (`// shim: <batch>`) exist only on integration branches and react-rules fails on them once the page's entry is gone. Gap protocol: a batch never edits a file it does not own; it files review/react-migration/requests/<batch>.md and the orchestrator applies requests between waves. Content freeze: while a page's integration branch is open, its src/app and src/scripts files on main change only through the orchestrator, who ports the change.

13. PARITY HARNESS (P0a): build-ref (cache, lock, atomic rename), static, runtime (canonical per-id DOM with whitespace-only text dropped, form-control properties, ?v= stripped, ECharts option/renderer/size hash plus foreign children and a sampled tooltip, _echarts_instance_ ignored; whole-body hash with id-less paths; masked viewport pixel diff; text, storage, URL, focus, scroll, canvas hashes, console, requests; --steps/--only/--estimate/--runs/--profile slow), faults (--data with expected tables, --islands with roots/affects, --shard), touched + slot-coverage, capture, dev-strict. Head and base builds both use GITHUB_SHA=parity00000.

14. ORCHESTRATION. The orchestrator prebuilds $BASE for each stage before a wave, runs at most three implementers at once, gives each worktree LL_NODE_MODULES (an absolute node_modules path: today the website-framework-github worktree, refreshed after P0a adds devDependencies), applies gap requests between waves, runs close batches one at a time, and runs full npm test, every page's runtime and dev-strict at each stage PR.

risks: Server-HTML drift from client islands (attribute order, `{" "}`, boolean attributes, select/option selected, input value). Mitigation: zero normalised-HTML diff per batch, locally and in CI.

Hydration mismatches that make React 19 client-render the root. Mitigation: R2/R3, useHydrated gating, react-rules bans (url()/asset()/SITE need useHydrated), the console check fails on any hydration warning.

Behaviour drift behind 'same final DOM' (repaint triggers, lazy timing, focus, scroll, hover cross-effects). Mitigation: per-step snapshots with focus, scroll, URL, canvas hashes, body hash and pixel diff; PAINT_TRIGGERS copied from call sites; known bugs reproduced deliberately.

Legacy and React coexisting on Week 4 and Week 3 integration branches. Mitigation: ownership marked at commit through ref callbacks; compat observers skip owned nodes; bridges confined to their folder and deleted by their replacing batch; whole-page parity after every batch.
Slot coverage gaps found late. Mitigation: touched.mjs + slot-coverage.mjs gates in the prep batches and W4-0c; later gaps through the gap protocol.

Payload growth (69 Week 4 Terms as client references, island props, painters in page chunks). Mitigation: static.mjs fails on HTML gzip growth over 2% per page and reports chunk bytes; heavy builders may load through import() inside effects; the owner sees cumulative sizes per stage PR.
StrictMode double effects in dev (duplicate vendor scripts, ECharts instances, WebGL contexts, listeners). Mitigation: module caches, hook-owned teardown, dev-strict.mjs per stage.

Nondeterminism (WebGL, ECharts animation, flow timer, Math.random order, network timing in hoverTips). Mitigation: reduced motion, seeded random, pinned Date, WebGL size-only, ECharts by option, --runs 3 with a slow profile and font-delay runs recorded in base.json.
Agent time limits. Mitigation: cached and locked base builds, --estimate/--steps/--shard, background builds with polling, at most three concurrent implementers.
